contract: CONTRACT: rule ids are frozen; changes are additive only (AGENTS.md).

rules.title: Money representation
rules.rule: All amounts are int64 CAD cents. Hourly rates are int cents per hour. Every rate and percentage (tax, FX, discount, markup, split share, surcharge, contingency, interest) is int parts-per-million (1% = 10000 ppm; 13% = 130000; 9.975% = 99750); one unit across all docs (CF-01). Columns end in _ppm. No float or numeric-with-fraction column holds money. Every division uses rhu(num, den).
rules.test: rate 9.975% stored as 99750; rhu(200000*99750, 1e6) = 19950; discount 10% stored as 100000

rules.title: Rounding mode: half away from zero, at fixed points only
rules.rule: rhu = round half away from zero (0.5 -> 1, -0.5 -> -1). Rounding happens only at: (1) time line amount, (2) percent discount / markup / surcharge / contingency, (3) each tax line, once per bill on the summed taxable base (never per line), (4) pro-rata tax share in an allocation, (5) cumulative interest per posting (BIL-C-072). Never round an intermediate that feeds another rounding. Banker's rounding is not used: each value is rounded once, so its bias advantage does not apply; half away from zero matches b2-sales-tax BIL-T-040 and what clients and Clio expect, and a bill a client re-computes by hand must match.
rules.source: design; b2-sales-tax rounding + BIL-T-040 (same half-away-from-zero rule)

rules.title: Rate resolution chain (fixed order, not configurable)
rules.rule: First hit wins: 1 manual rate on the entry (needs time.rates or user override right); 2 flat activity amount; 3 matter rate for the user; 4 matter rate for the user's role group (incl. a named rate table assigned to the matter); 5 client rate for the user; 6 client rate for the role group (incl. client rate table); 7 activity-category custom hourly rate; 8 user default rate. Store rate_cents and rate_source on the entry; rate_source in {manual, flat_activity, matter_user, matter_role, client_user, client_role, activity, user_default}. This reconciles the brief (matter > client > user group > user default) with time.json (manual > flat > matter > client/table > activity > default) and Clio's documented chain; user-before-group within each level.
rules.test: BIL-X-002: matter-role $175 beats client-user $182 and user default $200

rules.title: Rate effective date
rules.rule: The rate is the one effective on the work date (TimeEntry.date). A rate change re-prices only unbilled entries dated on or after its effective_from. Firm setting rate_basis = work_date (default) | bill_date; bill_date re-resolves at draft build.
rules.test: rate $400 -> $425 effective 2026-09-01; entry dated 2026-08-31 billed on 2026-09-30 at $400

rules.title: Manual override survives a matter move
rules.rule: Moving an entry to another matter re-resolves tiers 2-8; a manual rate (tier 1) is kept and flagged rate_recheck=true until a user with time.rates confirms it.
rules.test: entry manual $300 moved to matter with matter rate $250: rate stays $300, flag set

rules.title: Time rounding per entry, at save
rules.rule: billed_minutes = round(raw_minutes, increment, mode) at save; increment in {1, 6, 15} minutes, mode in {up, nearest(half-up)}. increment and mode are copied onto the entry. Bills never re-round. A settings change applies to entries saved after it.

rules.title: Time line amount
rules.rule: amount_cents = rhu(billed_minutes * rate_cents, 60). Hours displayed = billed_minutes/60 to 2 decimals (display only).

rules.title: Minimum entry
rules.rule: If raw_minutes > 0 and billed_minutes < minimum_entry, billed_minutes = minimum_entry (default 0 = off).

rules.title: Write-down and write-up never change recorded minutes
rules.rule: TimeEntry.minutes and billed_minutes are the accepted record (G9). A WriteDown row (original, adjusted, reason, stage) changes the bill line amount only. Pre-bill write-down: G9d / G-B1; above firm threshold also the owner role.
rules.test: 3.4 h x $425 = $1,445.00 adjusted to $1,200.00: entry minutes stay 204

rules.title: Write-up
rules.rule: Allowed only as a separate 'value adjustment' bill line with reason code, added by the responsible lawyer at G-B1, flagged to the approver at G-B2; never raises minutes or rate. Not allowed on contingency or flat lines.
rules.source: LSO Rules of Professional Conduct r.3.6-1 (https://lso.ca/about-lso/legislation-rules/rules-of-professional-conduct/chapter-3) (fees fair and reasonable)
rules.test: adjustment +$200.00 with reason 'urgency premium per retainer s.4' -> line shown; without reason -> rejected

rules.title: Order of reductions on a draft
rules.rule: 1 line write-down/up; 2 line discount; 3 bill discount on its eligible base (fees + own-cost lines | fees only | one line; never agent disbursements, b2 BIL-T-042); 4 tax on the reduced base; 5 after approval only: trust application, payments, client credit, credit notes. The spec's 'after credit notes' is moot because credit notes never exist on a draft (BIL-C-080).
rules.source: billing.json invoice-editor Discount order; Clio discounts (r05)
rules.test: BIL-X-005: $1,445 -> $1,200 write-down, then $100 fixed discount, then HST on $1,460.00

rules.title: Discount amount
rules.rule: percent: rhu(eligible_base * ppm, 1e6); fixed: min(amount, eligible_base). A discount never makes a line negative.

rules.title: Spread of a bill discount
rules.rule: Spread over eligible lines by largest remainder on weight = line net amount; ties go to the earliest line (sort_order). The spread is stored per line (discount_share) and drives tax buckets and realization.

rules.title: Write-down reason codes
rules.rule: reason in {duplicate, inefficiency, training, courtesy, over_estimate, scope, other}; 'other' needs text. show_on_bill true prints 'courtesy discount'.

rules.title: No discount after approval
rules.rule: Approved bills are immutable; any reduction after approval is a credit note (G-B5).
rules.test: PATCH discount on approved bill -> 409 bill_immutable

rules.title: Flat fee
rules.rule: Flat lines come from FeeArrangement (amount or milestone %: rhu(flat * ppm, 1e6)). Time on a flat matter is tracked non-billable and prints at $0 when show_on_bill. A flat activity on a flat-fee matter raises a double-charge warning.

rules.title: Out-of-scope work
rules.rule: On a hybrid arrangement, entries tagged out_of_scope are billed hourly per BIL-C-003; on a pure flat arrangement they are blocked from the bill until a change-of-scope letter is approved.

rules.title: Contingency fee
rules.rule: fee = rhu(recovery_base * pct_ppm, 1e6), pct may step by stage. recovery_base is a stored field on the matter's settlement record = damages + costs recovered - disbursements designated in the settlement - taxes; BIL-C-032 and BIL-C-033 both read it. No interim fee bill unless the agreement allows it. The agreement must be the LSO standard form unless the business-client exception applies.
rules.source: O. Reg. 563/20 Contingency Fee Agreements (https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/200563) (sections: verify)

rules.title: Contingency cap
rules.rule: Refuse approval (409 CFA_FEE_EXCEEDS_RECOVERY) if fee, excluding disbursements and taxes, exceeds recovery_base (BIL-C-032). Same formula as b1 BIL-L-020.
rules.source: O. Reg. 563/20 Contingency Fee Agreements (https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/200563) s.1 per b1 BIL-L-020
rules.test: settlement $30,000 incl. costs $5,000 and disbursements $2,000 -> recovery_base $28,000; fee $29,000 -> 409; capped proposal $28,000

rules.title: Disbursement tax class
rules.rule: Expense.agency = agent (paid as the client's agent: no HST on rebill) | own (firm's cost: HST on rebill amount). Default per category table; tax adviser must confirm the table before launch.
rules.source: CRA GST/HST Policy P-209R Lawyers' disbursements (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/forms-publications/publications/p-209r/lawyers-disbursements.html); b2-sales-tax BIL-T-030..033
rules.test: court filing fee $229.00 agent -> no HST; photocopies $86.40 own -> HST $11.23 share

rules.title: Markup
rules.rule: Markup ppm applies to own (soft) costs only; never to agent disbursements. markup = rhu(cost * ppm, 1e6); markup is taxable with the cost. Default 0.
rules.source: time.json expenses; LSO Rules of Professional Conduct r.3.6-1 (https://lso.ca/about-lso/legislation-rules/rules-of-professional-conduct/chapter-3)

rules.title: Disbursements paid from trust
rules.rule: An expense paid by trust withdrawal (G11) is listed on the bill in 'Paid from trust' and is excluded from amount due and AR.
rules.test: bill with $1,200 trust-paid filing fees: amount due unchanged

rules.title: Foreign currency expense
rules.rule: Store original amount and currency plus CAD cents = rhu(original_minor * fx_ppm, 1e6) at a recorded rate and date.

rules.title: Trust applied to fees
rules.rule: Allowed only when bill.delivered_at is set. amount <= min(bill balance - reserved_cents (BIL-C-054), trust available_cents of the same client-matter ledger (BIL-C-053)). For a combined client bill, only lines of that matter. Proposal does not touch AR. The trust row and both journals (BIL-J-008) post at execution, txn_date = executed_on; bank confirmation only matches the bank line.
rules.test: BIL-X-006: $3,000.00 against delivered bill; undelivered bill -> 409 bill_not_delivered

rules.title: Trust never overdraws
rules.rule: Authorization and execution each lock the client_ledger row (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE) and require available_cents >= amount; otherwise 409 trust_overdraw. Concurrent authorizations against the same funds therefore serialize and the second fails.
rules.test: ledger $2,000.00, request $2,000.01 -> 409 trust_overdraw; BIL-X-023: two $3,000 authorizations on $5,000 -> second 409

rules.title: Auto-apply setting proposes only
rules.rule: auto_apply_trust_on_approval creates a TrustFeeTransfer in 'proposed'; G-B4/G11 still required.
rules.test: setting on, bill approved: proposal exists, ledger unchanged

rules.title: Trust available balance
rules.rule: available_cents(ledger) = sum(posted rows with cleared_on <= today; receipts not yet cleared excluded) - protected_cents - minimum_balance_cents - sum(amount of withdrawal_request/TrustFeeTransfer in status authorized for that ledger). Every fee transfer, disbursement and refund from trust checks it under the ledger row lock at authorization and at execution.
rules.test: BIL-X-023; cheque receipt $5,000 uncleared, fee withdrawal $1,000 -> 409 uncleared_funds; protected $2,000 on $5,000, withdrawal $3,000.01 -> 409 trust_overdraw

rules.title: Bill reservation for authorized fee transfers
rules.rule: bill.reserved_cents = sum of fee transfers for the bill in authorized or executed-not-yet-applied. A new fee transfer needs amount <= balance - reserved_cents; payment and client-credit allocation to the bill is capped at balance - reserved_cents, the excess goes to unapplied then client credit (BIL-C-063). Cancelling an authorized transfer releases its reservation.
rules.test: BIL-X-023: bill $5,086.76, $3,000 reserved, card $2,500 -> $2,086.76 allocated, $413.24 excess

rules.title: Executed fee transfer above the bill balance
rules.rule: If at application an executed fee transfer exceeds the bill balance, apply the balance, post the excess to OP-2300 Due to trust and create a G6 return-to-trust task due the same day.
rules.test: BIL-X-024: $3,000 executed, balance $2,500 -> $500 due to trust

rules.title: Allocation within a bill (default fees_first)
rules.rule: Principal before interest: a payment first pays open principal (pre-tax + tax), then interest. Tax share per BIL-C-202. Pre-tax part order: fees, then own-cost disbursements, then agent disbursements. Alternative 'proportional' spreads the pre-tax part over the three buckets by largest remainder. Changing it is a G-B8 settings change effective for payments posted after it. The order is for revenue and fee-credit reporting; tax collected is unaffected (b2 BIL-T-082).

rules.title: Pre-tax part fills buckets in order
rules.rule: pre = P - tax share; fee bucket takes min(pre, fee_open), the rest goes to dtx, then dnt. Stored per allocation row (fee, dtx, dnt, tax, interest) so reversals mirror it exactly.

rules.title: Allocation across bills (default oldest_due_first)
rules.rule: A payment through a bill link or naming a bill number goes to that bill (excess per BIL-C-063). Otherwise order by (due_date, delivered_at, bill number) of the same client's open bills. Settings: oldest_due_first | proportional | manual. Payment plans use the same default and may be overridden per plan.
rules.source: billing.json payments-inbox, payment-plans; Clio payment plans (r06)

rules.title: Overpayment
rules.rule: Excess goes to ClientCredit (OP-2200) for that client under G-B3 (while G-B3 is pending it is an unapplied allocation, CF-13). Never to another client. Client credit is client money, not earned fees, so it is short-lived (BIL-C-067).

rules.title: Refund
rules.rule: Refund <= client credit; to the original method up to its captured amount, else by cheque/EFT from operating; G-B6 by a lawyer not the requester.

rules.title: Reversal (chargeback, NSF, failed PAD)
rules.rule: Reverse every allocation of the payment with its stored bucket split, recompute bill status; fees debited to operating. A reversal of a trust deposit always opens a trust exception; in the same DB transaction, only if the ledger would go negative, insert a receipt from the firm general account for exactly the shortfall (G6) with Dr OP-1100 receivable from client (or OP-6100) / Cr OP-1000.
rules.test: BIL-X-020: bill back to $2,086.76; BIL-X-026: shortfall 300000 replenished, ledger 0; ledger with 500000 -> reversal only

rules.title: Applying client credit
rules.rule: Same client only, to delivered bills, G-B3; allocated like a payment (BIL-C-060).

rules.title: Client credit is short-lived
rules.rule: Within client_credit_max_business_days (firm setting, default 5, verify against By-Law 9) of creation, client credit must be (a) applied to a delivered bill of the same client under G-B3 with client direction, (b) refunded under G-B6, or (c) transferred to trust under G6 (BIL-J-019). A daily aging job opens a trust exception 'client money in operating' for credit older than the limit.
rules.source: b1 BIL-L-042; LSO By-Law 9 (https://lso.ca/about-lso/legislation-rules/by-laws/by-law-9) money belonging to a client received in the general account (verify provision and time limit)
rules.test: BIL-X-025: $240 created 2026-10-07, open on 2026-10-15 -> exception task

rules.title: Provider events apply by state precedence
rules.rule: Dedup on (provider, event_id). Handlers re-fetch the provider object by provider_ref and set payment state by precedence pending < received < posted < partially_refunded < refunded; reversed is terminal. Order of arrival does not matter; a lower-precedence event after a higher one is a no-op.
rules.test: dispute event before capture -> payment created then reversed once; capture replayed after refund -> no change

rules.title: Interest start and method
rules.rule: Simple interest, actual/365, on open principal (bill total excluding interest, less principal allocations, credit notes and write-offs) for each day in [start, paid_date). start = max(due_date, months_after(delivery_local_date, 1)) (BIL-C-073). No interest on interest.
rules.source: Solicitors Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. S.15 (https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90s15) s.33(1); b1 BIL-L-008

rules.title: Interest rate source
rules.rule: Charged only at a rate the client agreed in writing, printed on the bill. The rate is snapshotted to bill.interest_rate_ppm at approval; later profile changes affect only later bills. A firm may set its agreed rate equal to a CJA s.127 published rate as a benchmark, but the Act supplies no default rate. Default: off.
rules.source: Solicitors Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. S.15 (https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90s15) s.33(3),(5); b1 BIL-L-009, BIL-L-010; Courts of Justice Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. C.43, s.127 (https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90c43)
rules.test: retainer silent, profile 6% -> interest 0 and agent warning

rules.title: Interest posting
rules.rule: Interest is not a bill line on an approved bill. It accrues in InterestCharge rows posted at each month end and at payoff/credit/write-off, shown on statements and reminders, and may be carried as a non-taxable line on the next bill (BIL-C-204). Cumulative method: posting_k = rhu(sum over principal segments of principal_i * rate_ppm * days_i, 1e6 * 365) from interest start to the posting date, minus the sum of prior postings; a segment ends at each allocation, credit or write-off. Total charged always equals the one-shot figure.
rules.test: BIL-X-009: 2026-11-30 posts $9.95 (29 days); payoff posts $14.75 - $9.95 = $4.80; total exactly $14.75

rules.title: Dates for billing clocks
rules.rule: delivery_local_date = delivered_at AT TIME ZONE 'America/Toronto'. One-month windows use months_after(local_date, n) (same day n months later, clamped to month end, b1 BIL-L-003/004); day windows use days_after(local_date, n); the two never share code. Interest accrues for days >= months_after(d, 1); suit (Solicitors Act s.2) is allowed on days > months_after(d, 1) until counsel confirms otherwise.
rules.source: Solicitors Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. S.15 (https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90s15) ss.2, 33; Legislation Act, 2006, S.O. 2006, c. 21, Sched. F, s.89 (verify); b1 BIL-L-003, BIL-L-004

rules.title: Credit notes never edit bills
rules.rule: A credit note references one bill (one payer bill on split), has its own gapless sequence assigned at issue, kind in {fee_reduction, billing_error, bad_debt_write_off, refund}, and lists pre-tax per bucket and tax per tax line.

rules.title: Where a credit goes
rules.rule: First reduces open AR of the bill. Excess goes back to the sources of payment: trust-sourced allocations first (OP-2300 Due to trust, repaid by a trust receipt under G6 the same day), then client credit (OP-2200), which follows BIL-C-067.
rules.source: billing.json credit-notes (refunds of trust-paid fees go back to trust first); LSO By-Law 9 (https://lso.ca/about-lso/legislation-rules/by-laws/by-law-9) (verify)

rules.title: Credit limits
rules.rule: Per bucket: credited pre-tax <= billed pre-tax minus prior credits and write-offs.
rules.test: bill fees $1,000, prior CN $900, new CN $200 -> 409 credit_exceeds_bill

rules.title: Void
rules.rule: Draft/pending: discard (no number). Approved and delivered_at null: void under G-B2 (billing.approve, not the preparer) keeps number, posts exact reversal of the approval entry dated the void date, unlocks entries to approved; no credit note. delivered_at not null: 409 bill_delivered_use_credit_note (use POST /credit-notes). a2 voidBill must match.
rules.test: BIL-X-018; void on delivered bill -> 409 bill_delivered_use_credit_note

rules.title: Write-off of a balance
rules.rule: G-B5 (lawyer other than requester; owner role above threshold). Writes off all open buckets; open tax gives the bad-debt adjustment (BIL-C-205).

rules.title: Recovery after write-off
rules.rule: A payment on a written_off bill (billing.payments, G-B3) stays on that bill, up to the written-off amount: tax part = rhu(recovered * bill_tax, bill_total) per tax line, posted Cr OP-2100 in the recovery period; pre-tax part Cr OP-6100 (BIL-J-018). Status stays written_off; recovered_cents is tracked.

rules.title: Split shares
rules.rule: BillSplit share_ppm per payer, sum = 1000000, payer order = sort_order (first payer = lowest). applies_to = all | fees | disbursements; non-covered lines go to the client payer.

rules.title: Split per line with cumulative carry
rules.rule: Lines in sort_order; C_k = cumulative line amount through line k. Non-first payer p on line k = floor(C_k * share_ppm_p / 1e6) - amount already assigned to p; first payer takes the rest of the line. If the first payer's part would be negative (a line smaller than payers - 1 cents), cut the non-first parts from the last payer backwards; the cut carries to later lines. Each non-first payer ends within 1 cent of its share of the bill, so the first payer no longer absorbs a cent per line.

rules.title: Payer bills are independent
rules.rule: Each payer bill has its own number, tax computation (BIL-C-200), allocations, interest and aging; trust of one payer is never applied to another payer's bill.

rules.title: Surcharge eligibility
rules.rule: Only when all hold: firm setting on; card-network notice date passed; surcharge-free method offered; card funding = credit (not debit, prepaid, wallet); destination = operating; firm not in Quebec and card billing address not in Quebec; LSO position check attached at enable. Otherwise surcharge = 0.
rules.source: Card-network surcharge rules for Canada as published by processors (Clio Canada surcharging article, research r05/r06); Quebec Consumer Protection Act CQLR c P-40.1 (verify section); LSO position (verify)
rules.test: Visa debit -> 0; Quebec billing address -> 0; retainer to trust -> 0

rules.title: Surcharge amount
rules.rule: surcharge_ppm <= min(24000, cost_of_acceptance_ppm); surcharge = rhu(amount_applied * ppm, 1e6); shown as its own receipt line with the percent, plus its tax (BIL-C-208). Feature flag surcharge_enabled ships off until BIL-C-208 and CF-18 are verified.
rules.source: Card-network surcharge rules for Canada as published by processors (Clio Canada surcharging article, research r05/r06); Quebec Consumer Protection Act CQLR c P-40.1 (verify section)

rules.title: Refund of a surcharged payment
rules.rule: A refund of part or all of a surcharged payment refunds the surcharge and its tax pro rata: surcharge_refund = rhu(surcharge * refunded, amount_applied), tax per line = rhu(surcharge_tax * refunded, amount_applied); a full refund returns exactly the remaining surcharge and tax.

rules.title: Batch billing
rules.rule: Each draft is built in its own transaction with idempotency key (batch_run_id, matter_id | client_id, period_to). Matters under minimum_bill_cents are skipped and listed. Drafts go to G-B1; nothing is auto-approved. Cut-off: entries dated <= cutoff (default) or created <= cutoff.
rules.test: re-running run R1 creates 0 new drafts; one matter failing does not roll back others

rules.title: Combined client bill
rules.rule: Lines grouped by matter; per-matter subtotals; tax computed once on the whole bill; trust applied per matter subtotal only.
rules.source: billing.json open question; trust per matter
rules.test: matter A $1,000 owed, matter B ledger $5,000 -> B trust cannot pay A lines

rules.title: Bill numbering
rules.rule: Number assigned in the approval transaction from a per-firm sequence row (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE), format prefix-YYYY-NNNN; gapless; voided numbers kept. Credit notes use their own sequence.
rules.test: two concurrent approvals get 0147 and 0148, never the same

rules.title: Bill date = approval date
rules.rule: Bill date is the approval date (Toronto). HST is reported in the period of the bill date.
rules.test: approved 2026-09-30 23:30 Toronto, delivered 2026-10-01 -> HST in September

rules.title: Delivery starts the clocks
rules.rule: delivered_at is set only by the delivery effect handler on evidence (email provider accepted + message-id, portal first view, or clerk-entered mailing date with proof), only from null to a value <= now(), and never changed after (corrections are an audited delivery_correction under G-B2). It drives trust application eligibility, interest start, aging buckets, suit and assessment windows, always via delivery_local_date (BIL-C-073). A bounce leaves delivered_at null.
rules.source: Solicitors Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. S.15 (https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90s15) ss.2, 3, 4 (verify electronic delivery)
rules.test: bounced email: trust proposal stays not_eligible

rules.title: Void across tax periods
rules.rule: A void reverses on the void date. If the bill-date period is already filed, the reversal is a negative adjustment in the void period; a void in the same unfiled period nets to zero. Preflight warning W-PERIOD-CROSS for any approved bill still undelivered at period end.
rules.test: BIL-X-031: approved 2026-09-30, Q3 filed, void 2026-10-05 -> Q4 adjustment -$130.00

rules.title: Tax once per bill per tax line
rules.rule: For each tax line: tax = rhu(sum(taxable line net after discounts) * rate_ppm, 1e6). Never per line. Rates from TaxRate rows effective on the tax point.
rules.source: b2-sales-tax BIL-T-040, BIL-T-001, BIL-T-002; CRA GST/HST rates (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/tax/businesses/topics/gst-hst-businesses/charge-collect-which-rate/calculator.html)

rules.title: Approval preconditions for tax
rules.rule: Approval refused if the firm GST/HST registration number is missing or invalid, or place of supply is not confirmed by the lawyer.
rules.source: b2-sales-tax BIL-T-010, BIL-T-060, BIL-T-061; b1 BIL-L-047

rules.title: Tax share of every allocation is proportional
rules.rule: Each principal allocation P on a bill carries tax = rhu(P * tax_open, principal_open) where principal_open = open pre-tax + open tax; an allocation that clears principal takes the exact remaining tax. The pre-tax part then follows BIL-C-061. With two tax lines, split the tax share by largest remainder over open tax per line.

rules.title: Credit note tax (single rule for b2 and b3)
rules.rule: Per tax line: tax = rhu(credit_pre_tax * line_tax, bill_taxable_base), using the source bill's tax lines and rates; a credit that exhausts the remaining taxable base takes exactly the remaining tax.
rules.test: BIL-X-011: $0.44, $0.44, then remainder $0.43; base 5 c, tax 1 c, credit 3 c -> tax 1 c (rate x credit would give 0 and lets credits exceed bill tax)

rules.title: No tax on interest
rules.rule: Interest charges for late payment carry no GST/HST and appear on their own non-taxable line. Card surcharges are not covered here (BIL-C-208).
rules.source: b2-sales-tax BIL-T-043; b1 BIL-L-049; ETA s.161

rules.title: Bad-debt tax adjustment
rules.rule: On write-off, tax adjustment = open tax of the bill (which equals rhu(bill_tax * written_off, bill_total) because BIL-C-202 keeps allocations proportional); posted in the period of write-off. Recovery later re-includes tax proportionally (BIL-C-086).

rules.title: Two-line taxes
rules.rule: GST + QST/PST: each line on the same pre-tax base, rounded separately, no tax on tax; provincial line only if the firm holds that registration.

rules.title: Place of supply changed after approval
rules.rule: Before delivery: void and rebuild (new number). After delivery: full credit note + new bill. Replaces the spec's 'returns to draft', which would break approved-bill immutability.
rules.test: ON bill $1,130.00 delivered, client is QC (firm QST-registered) -> CN $1,130.00 + new bill $1,149.75

rules.title: Card surcharge is taxable (verify)
rules.rule: A card surcharge is extra consideration for the supply being paid, so it is taxed at the paid bill's tax lines: per tax line, surcharge_tax = rhu(surcharge * line_tax, bill_total - bill_tax), i.e. the bill's effective rate on its pre-tax total (agency disbursements dilute it). Same rule as b2 BIL-T-044. (verify with CRA GST/HST guidance before enabling.)
rules.source: b2-sales-tax BIL-T-044 (verify); Excise Tax Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. E-15 (https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/acts/E-15/)
